title: Revelation Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Revelation chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Revelation Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Revelation Chapter 21.

questions.question: In Revelation 21, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: A new heaven and a new earth
The tabernacle of God with men
questions.correctAnswer: A new heaven and a new earth
questions.explanation: The first event mentioned in the chapter is the vision of a new heaven and a new earth, as stated in Revelation 21:1.

questions.question: What did John see coming down from God out of heaven?
questions.correctAnswer: The holy city, new Jerusalem
questions.explanation: John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven as described in Revelation 21:2.

questions.question: What will God do to the tears of His people?
options: He will wipe away all tears
questions.correctAnswer: He will wipe away all tears
questions.explanation: According to Revelation 21:4, God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes.

questions.question: What is promised to those who overcome?
options: They will receive a new name
questions.correctAnswer: They shall inherit all things
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:7 states that he that overcometh shall inherit all things.

questions.question: What is described as not existing anymore in Revelation 21?
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: In Revelation 21:1 and 21:4, it states there was no more sea, and God shall wipe away all tears, indicating there shall be no more death, sorrow, or crying.

questions.question: Who will dwell with men according to the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: God
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:3 states that God will dwell with men and they shall be His people.

questions.question: What phrase does the one sitting on the throne use to describe His authority?
questions.correctAnswer: I am Alpha and Omega
questions.explanation: In Revelation 21:6, it is said, 'I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end.'

questions.question: What will be given to him that is athirst?
options: The fountain of the water of life
questions.correctAnswer: The fountain of the water of life
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:6 mentions that He will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely.

questions.question: What is the fate of the fearful and unbelieving according to Revelation 21?
options: They shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire
questions.correctAnswer: They shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:8 states that the fearful and unbelieving shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone.

questions.question: Who is referred to as 'the bride, the Lamb's wife'?
questions.correctAnswer: The holy city
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:9 indicates that the angel came to show John the bride, the Lamb's wife, which refers to the holy city, new Jerusalem.

questions.question: What did the one who sat upon the throne command John to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Write
questions.explanation: In Revelation 21:5, the one that sat upon the throne commanded John to write.

questions.question: Does Revelation 21 mention that there will be no more pain?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:4 states that there shall be no more pain.

questions.question: Is God described as being with His people in Revelation 21?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: According to Revelation 21:3, God will dwell with men and be their God.

questions.question: Does Revelation 21 say that the new Jerusalem is coming down from the earth?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:2 states that the new Jerusalem is coming down from God out of heaven, not from the earth.

questions.question: Is the lake of fire mentioned as a place for the righteous?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:8 states that the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone is for the fearful and unbelieving, not the righteous.

medium.title: Revelation Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Revelation Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What precious stone is the light of the holy Jerusalem compared to in Revelation 21:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Jasper stone, clear as crystal
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:11 describes the light of the holy Jerusalem as being like a jasper stone, clear as crystal.

questions.question: What does Revelation 21:14 promise will happen if someone is part of the twelve apostles named on the city's foundations described in Revelation 21:12?
options: They are represented as foundations of the city
They will enter the twelve gates guarded by angels
They will receive a golden reed to measure the city
They will dwell on the great and high mountain
questions.correctAnswer: They are represented as foundations of the city
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:14 states the wall of the city had twelve foundations with the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb, following the mention of the twelve gates and tribes in verse 12.

questions.question: According to Revelation 21:16, what is unique about the city's measurements?
options: The length, breadth, and height are equal
The city is taller than it is wide
The city has no height mentioned
The city is twice as long as it is broad
questions.correctAnswer: The length, breadth, and height are equal
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:16 explains that the city lieth foursquare, and the length, breadth, and height are equal.

questions.question: What measurement does the angel use to measure the city and its walls in Revelation 21:15-17?
options: A golden reed according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel
A silver rod according to the measure of the earth
A measuring tape from the throne of God
A staff of iron given by the Lamb
questions.correctAnswer: A golden reed according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:15-17 describes the measuring of the city with a golden reed according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.

questions.question: How many gates does the holy Jerusalem have, and how are they distributed according to Revelation 21:12-13?
options: Twelve gates, three on each side (east, north, south, west)
Ten gates, five on the east and five on the west
Seven gates, all on the east side
Four gates, one on each side
questions.correctAnswer: Twelve gates, three on each side (east, north, south, west)
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:12-13 states the city had twelve gates, with three gates on the east, north, south, and west each.

questions.question: What is the material of the city's wall as described in Revelation 21:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Jasper
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:18 describes the wall of the city as being built of jasper.

questions.question: According to Revelation 21:10, from where does the holy Jerusalem descend?
questions.correctAnswer: Out of heaven from God
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:10 states that the holy Jerusalem descends out of heaven from God.

questions.question: What role do the twelve angels have at the gates of the city in Revelation 21:12?
options: They stand at the gates, with names of the twelve tribes written thereon
They measure the city with a golden reed
They carry the glory of God
They adorn the city like a bride
questions.correctAnswer: They stand at the gates, with names of the twelve tribes written thereon
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:12 mentions twelve angels at the gates, with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel written on the gates.

questions.question: What does the city's purity and appearance symbolize in practical Christian living according to Revelation 21:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness and transparency before God
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:18 describes the city as pure gold, like clear glass, symbolizing holiness and transparency, which Christians are called to emulate in their lives.

questions.question: How does the foursquare design of the city in Revelation 21:16 reflect practical Christian values?
options: It represents completeness and stability in faith
It shows a focus on wealth accumulation
It indicates separation from the world
questions.correctAnswer: It represents completeness and stability in faith
questions.explanation: The foursquare shape with equal length, breadth, and height (Revelation 21:16) symbolizes wholeness and stability, qualities important in Christian living.

questions.question: What can Christians learn about God's presence from Revelation 21:3 in the context of the new Jerusalem described later?
options: God will dwell with His people and be their God
God will remain distant and mysterious
God will only dwell with angels
God will not interact with humanity anymore
questions.correctAnswer: God will dwell with His people and be their God
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:3 promises that God’s tabernacle is with men and He will dwell with them, which is fulfilled in the description of the holy Jerusalem in later verses.

questions.question: What does the measurement of the city’s wall being 144 cubits symbolize in Revelation 21:17?
options: God’s perfect measurement and divine standard
An earthly city’s typical wall size
questions.correctAnswer: God’s perfect measurement and divine standard
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:17 notes the wall is 144 cubits, measured by the angel, symbolizing divine perfection and order in God’s kingdom.

questions.question: According to Revelation 21:10-11, how does the glory of God manifest in the holy Jerusalem?
options: Her light is like a precious jasper stone, clear as crystal
The city is dark and hidden
The city is surrounded by fire
The city is covered in clouds
questions.correctAnswer: Her light is like a precious jasper stone, clear as crystal
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:11 says the city has the glory of God, and its light is like a jasper stone, clear as crystal, showing the manifestation of God's glory.

questions.question: True or False: Revelation 21:3 promises that God will dwell with men and be their God in the new heaven and new earth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:3 clearly states that the tabernacle of God is with men, and He will dwell with them and be their God.

questions.question: True or False: The wall of the holy city is described as being made of pure gold like clear glass in Revelation 21:18.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:18 says the wall is made of jasper, while the city itself is pure gold like clear glass, not the wall.

hard.title: Revelation Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Revelation Chapter 21.

questions.question: Which precious stone is described as the first foundation of the wall of the city in Revelation 21:19?
questions.correctAnswer: jasper
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:19 states, 'The first foundation was jasper,' indicating jasper as the first foundation stone.

questions.question: How many foundations adorned with precious stones are described in Revelation 21:19-20?
questions.correctAnswer: Twelve
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:19-20 lists twelve foundations, each with a different precious stone, making twelve foundations in total.

questions.question: According to Revelation 21:21, what material are the twelve gates of the city made from?
questions.correctAnswer: Pearls
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:21 says, 'And the twelve gates were twelve pearls; every several gate was of one pearl.'

questions.question: What is said about the temple in the New Jerusalem in Revelation 21:22?
options: There is no temple; the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple
The temple is made of gold
The temple is located at the city center
The temple is made of precious stones
questions.correctAnswer: There is no temple; the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:22 states, 'And I saw no temple therein: for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it.'

questions.question: Why does the city in Revelation 21:23 have no need for the sun or the moon?
options: Because the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof
questions.correctAnswer: Because the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:23 explains that 'the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.'

questions.question: According to Revelation 21:27, who is permitted to enter the city?
options: Those written in the Lamb's book of life
questions.correctAnswer: Those written in the Lamb's book of life
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:27 states, 'But they which are written in the Lamb's book of life' shall enter, and nothing defiling or lying shall enter.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'jasper' (ἴασπις) in Revelation 21:19 specifically refer to?
options: A precious stone, often a variety of quartz
questions.correctAnswer: A precious stone, often a variety of quartz
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'jasper' (ἴασπις) in Revelation 21:19 refers to a precious stone, generally a variety of quartz known for its hardness and beauty.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Revelation 21:16, describing the city lying foursquare with equal length, breadth, and height?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:16 uses inclusio by framing the city’s dimensions equally in length, breadth, and height, marking completeness and perfection.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is thematically connected to Revelation 21:3 about God dwelling with men?
questions.correctAnswer: Leviticus 26:11-12
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:11-12 speaks of God dwelling among His people, paralleling Revelation 21:3 where God dwells with men as their God.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of Revelation 21:4 where God wipes away all tears and abolishes death and pain?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 25:8
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:8 prophesies that God will swallow up death forever and wipe away tears, echoing Revelation 21:4’s promise of no more death or sorrow.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Revelation 21:19, which describes the precious stones in the foundations of the wall?
options: Description of the measurement and construction of the wall
The twelve gates made of pearls
questions.correctAnswer: Description of the measurement and construction of the wall
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:18 precedes 21:19 and describes the building of the wall of jasper and the city being pure gold, setting context for the foundations described in 21:19.

questions.question: How does Revelation 21:25's statement about the gates never being shut relate to ancient city practices?
options: It symbolizes perpetual safety and the absence of night or evil
It indicates the city is undefended
It shows the gates are broken
It reflects a temporary state during a festival
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes perpetual safety and the absence of night or evil
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:25 states the gates will never be shut because 'there shall be no night there,' symbolizing eternal safety and holiness unlike earthly cities.

questions.question: What typological significance does the twelve gates of pearl in Revelation 21:21 have in relation to Old Testament symbolism?
options: Reflects the twelve tribes of Israel and divine perfection
Represents the twelve months of the year
questions.correctAnswer: Reflects the twelve tribes of Israel and divine perfection
questions.explanation: The twelve gates correspond to the twelve tribes of Israel (Revelation 21:12) and symbolize divine completeness and covenant fulfillment.

questions.question: Which literary device best describes the pattern of precious stones in the foundations of the city wall in Revelation 21:19-20?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: The listing of twelve precious stones in sequence in Revelation 21:19-20 demonstrates parallelism, a common Hebrew literary device for emphasis and structure.

questions.question: True or False: Revelation 21:24 states that the kings of the earth will bring their glory and honour into the New Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:24 explicitly says, 'the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it,' confirming the statement as true.

theological.title: Revelation Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Revelation Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Revelation 21:3 teach about God's relationship with redeemed humanity?
options: God will dwell with His people and be their God
God will remain distant but benevolent
God will judge His people from heaven
God will send angels to guide His people
questions.correctAnswer: God will dwell with His people and be their God
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:3 explicitly states that the tabernacle of God is with men, He will dwell with them, and be their God, indicating intimate fellowship between God and redeemed humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the final state of sin and death is taught in Revelation 21:4?
options: There will be no more death, sorrow, crying, or pain
Sin and death will continue but be diminished
Sorrow and pain will remain as tests of faith
Death will be transformed into a new form of existence
questions.correctAnswer: There will be no more death, sorrow, crying, or pain
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:4 clearly teaches that God will wipe away all tears and there will be no more death, sorrow, crying, or pain, signifying the complete removal of sin's effects in the new creation.

questions.question: What doctrine about eternal inheritance is presented in Revelation 21:7?
options: The overcomer shall inherit all things and be God's son
Inheritance is limited to earthly blessings
questions.correctAnswer: The overcomer shall inherit all things and be God's son
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:7 teaches that those who overcome will inherit all things and have a filial relationship with God, emphasizing salvation as sonship and eternal possession.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Revelation 21:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Eternality
questions.explanation: Verse 6 identifies God as Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, underscoring His eternal nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Revelation 21:5 when God declares, 'Behold, I make all things new'?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: God's declaration to make all things new in Revelation 21:5 reflects His sovereign power over creation and history.

questions.question: How does Revelation 21:22 connect to Old Testament temple theology?
options: It fulfills the temple’s purpose by identifying God and the Lamb as the temple
It suggests the temple will be rebuilt physically on earth
It denies the need for any temple or sanctuary
It replaces the temple with a new priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the temple’s purpose by identifying God and the Lamb as the temple
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:22 shows the fulfillment of the temple’s role as God's dwelling place by declaring the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb themselves are the temple, fulfilling tabernacle symbolism.

questions.question: In what way does Revelation 21:1 prepare the eschatological hope presented in Isaiah 65:17?
options: Both describe a new heaven and a new earth as God’s ultimate renewal
Both predict the destruction of the physical earth without replacement
Both focus on the restoration of the earthly temple only
Both emphasize a return to pre-Fall conditions without transformation
questions.correctAnswer: Both describe a new heaven and a new earth as God’s ultimate renewal
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:1 anticipates the new creation described in Isaiah 65:17, affirming God’s promise of ultimate cosmic renewal.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Revelation 21:8 and 21:27 teach about judgment and the final state of the unredeemed?
options: The unredeemed will be excluded from the new creation and suffer the second death
The unredeemed will coexist with believers in the new Jerusalem
Judgment is temporary and will eventually be reversed
The final judgment is symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: The unredeemed will be excluded from the new creation and suffer the second death
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 27 teach that those defiled and unrighteous will have their part in the lake of fire, the second death, and will not enter the holy city, indicating eternal separation.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of the New Jerusalem is taught by combining Revelation 21:18 and 21:21?
options: The city is both gloriously pure and symbolically precious
The city is a literal earthly metropolis made of common materials
The city represents a spiritual state with no physical reality
The city's materials indicate human craftsmanship
questions.correctAnswer: The city is both gloriously pure and symbolically precious
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:18 and 21:21 describe the city’s walls as jasper and the gates as pearls, symbolizing purity and divine glory rather than mere physical construction.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about God's covenant faithfulness emerges from Revelation 21:12 and 21:14?
options: God’s covenant people include both Israel and the apostles, uniting Old and New Testament promises
The city excludes Israel and focuses only on the Church
The apostles replace Israel in God’s plan
The foundations and gates represent political entities
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant people include both Israel and the apostles, uniting Old and New Testament promises
questions.explanation: Verse 12 names the twelve tribes of Israel on the gates, and verse 14 the twelve apostles on the foundations, showing continuity and fulfillment of God’s covenant people.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Revelation 21:1–2 depicts a purely symbolic vision lacking real future hope. What does the text actually teach?
options: It teaches a real, tangible new heaven and new earth with a holy city prepared as a bride
It is only symbolic language for spiritual principles without physical reality
It anticipates an earthly utopia achieved by human effort
It denies any future restoration or hope
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches a real, tangible new heaven and new earth with a holy city prepared as a bride
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 2 describe a new heaven and earth and the holy city coming down from God, indicating a tangible eschatological reality, not mere symbolism.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice and holiness is taught in Revelation 21:8?
options: The fearful, unbelieving, and sinful receive eternal punishment in the lake of fire
God ultimately pardons all sinners without judgment
The lake of fire is a metaphor for social exclusion only
questions.correctAnswer: The fearful, unbelieving, and sinful receive eternal punishment in the lake of fire
questions.explanation: Verse 8 clearly states that those who practice sin and unbelief have their part in the lake of fire, demonstrating God’s holiness and just judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is underscored by Revelation 21:23’s description of the city needing no sun or moon?
questions.correctAnswer: Glory
questions.explanation: Verse 23 says the city’s light comes from the glory of God and the Lamb, highlighting God's radiant glory as the source of illumination.

questions.question: How do Revelation 21:24 and 21:26 together illustrate the universal scope of salvation?
options: Nations and kings bring their glory and honor into the city, showing inclusivity
Only Israel is saved and honored in the city
Salvation excludes earthly rulers and nations
The city is limited to spiritual beings only
questions.correctAnswer: Nations and kings bring their glory and honor into the city, showing inclusivity
questions.explanation: Verses 24 and 26 describe the nations and kings of the earth bringing their glory into the city, emphasizing salvation’s global and inclusive reach.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about God's covenant and eschatological restoration is taught by Revelation 21:12 and 21:25?
options: God’s covenant people are secure and the gates never close because there is no night
The city is exclusive and gates close to protect from outsiders
The city has temporal security but vulnerable at night
The gates symbolize separation from God’s people
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant people are secure and the gates never close because there is no night
questions.explanation: Verse 12 speaks of gates named after tribes of Israel, and verse 25 states the gates are never shut because there is no night, signaling eternal security and openness.
